questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large labelled diagram to show a section through the mammalian skin. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*The diagram has to be drawn by the candidate.* A large, clear, pencil drawing of a vertical section through the skin, showing from top to bottom three layers, with a **title** ("Vertical section through mammalian skin") and **label lines** that do not cross.

**Elements to draw**
- **Epidermis** (top layer): the **cornified (horny) layer** of dead cells, and below it the **Malpighian (germinative) layer** of dividing cells containing **melanin** pigment; **hair shaft** coming out through the surface; a **pore** (opening of the sweat duct).
- **Dermis** (middle layer): **hair follicle** with the **hair root and bulb**; **erector (arrector pili) muscle** attached to the follicle; **sebaceous gland** opening into the follicle; **coiled sweat gland** with its **sweat duct** going up to the pore; **blood capillaries**, **arteriole** and **venule**; **nerve fibre** with **sensory receptors** (touch, pressure, heat and cold, pain).
- **Subcutaneous (fatty) layer** (bottom): **fat cells** (adipose tissue) that insulate the body.

**Labels expected** (at least 8): cornified layer, Malpighian layer, epidermis, dermis, hair shaft, hair follicle, sebaceous gland, sweat gland, sweat duct, pore, erector muscle, blood vessel, sensory nerve ending, fat layer.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How does the skin function in

(i) Protection *(5 marks)*

(ii) Secretion *(2 marks)*

(iii) Temperature regulation during over cooling. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Protection**
1. The **cornified layer** of dead cells, rich in **keratin**, protects the underlying tissues against **mechanical injury** (friction, knocks) and **entry of germs**.
2. It is **waterproof**, so it **prevents loss of water** from the body and also stops the entry of water.
3. **Melanin** in the Malpighian layer **absorbs ultraviolet rays** and protects deeper cells from sunlight damage.
4. **Sebum** from the sebaceous glands is **slightly acidic and antiseptic**, so it kills or slows the growth of bacteria and fungi on the skin.
5. **Hairs** protect the skin and trap a layer of air; the **fatty layer** acts as a cushion against shocks.

**(ii) Secretion**
- The **sweat glands secrete sweat** (water, mineral salts and a little urea) which cools the body and gets rid of some wastes.
- The **sebaceous glands secrete sebum** (an oily substance) which keeps the skin and hair soft, supple and waterproof.

**(iii) Temperature regulation during over cooling (when the body is too cold)**
The **hypothalamus** detects the fall in blood temperature and the **skin thermoreceptors** detect the cold. The skin then:
1. **Vasoconstriction**: the **arterioles in the dermis narrow**, so less blood flows near the surface and **less heat is lost** by radiation.
2. The **erector muscles contract** and the **hairs stand up**, trapping a thicker layer of **air (an insulator)** next to the skin (goose pimples).
3. The **sweat glands stop producing sweat**, so no heat is lost by evaporation.
4. **Shivering** (rapid muscle contractions) releases heat that warms the blood.
5. The **fatty layer** under the skin insulates the body and reduces heat loss.

The body temperature returns to normal (about 37 °C): **negative feedback**.
